dek.text: Lockheed Martin says Hadrian will bring a {{number:c4:1}} machine cell to its Grand Prairie plant. Hadrian says its own factories combine AI and robotics. The release never says what AI would do in this cell.

introduction.text: [Lockheed Martin made the announcement in a release datelined Dallas on {{date:c6}}](c6). [It says Hadrian will bring a highly automated machining cell to the Grand Prairie facility, run by Lockheed's own production workforce](c3). [The cell has {{number:c4:1}} machines and is expected to be operational early next year](c4). [The facility supports all of Lockheed's Missiles and Fire Control programs, among them PAC-{{number:c7}} MSE, THAAD, PrSM and JATM](c7). [A state accessibility filing puts the plant at {{number:c34}} West Marshall Drive in Dallas County](c34).

[The cell sits inside a {{money:c1}} million investment that Lockheed says will grow the operation past {{number:c1:1}} square feet](c1). [That includes {{number:c2}} square feet of new space and {{number:c2:1}} square feet of office space turned over to manufacturing](c2).

sections.heading: What Lockheed says it has already done

paragraphs.text: [In a few months the company says it turned former office space into manufacturing areas and installed more than {{number:c10}} high precision machines](c10). [It expects to have added nearly {{number:c11:1}} new advanced machines across the facility by the end of the year](c11).

[Nearly {{number:c12}} production employees work at the plant](c12). [The company says it made {{number:c12:1}} parts in {{number:c12:2}}](c12). [The release does not say whether the {{number:c4:1}} machines in Hadrian's cell count toward the nearly {{number:c11:1}}](c4).

[Hadrian describes its own factories as highly automated and combining process engineering, AI and robotics](c15). [Its home page calls its software Opus a full stack, AI powered platform for factory autonomy](c21). [Hadrian says Opus interprets legacy designs and automates manufacturing and inspection](c20).

[Hadrian chief executive Chris Power says the company is bringing the automation, software and workforce training from its own factories inside Lockheed Martin](c16). [Hadrian's home page also offers dedicated manufacturing or inspection cells deployed at customer sites](c22). The release does not name Opus. It does not say whether any of the cell's machines will use AI, or for what.
[The announcement follows a seven year agreement the two companies signed in {{number:c13}}](c13).

[Lockheed says it plans to create {{number:c5}} jobs across the United States, {{number:c5:1}} of them in Texas](c5). Those are the company's own figures. The release gives no count for the Grand Prairie plant alone.
